title: FCI Leavenworth Elevator & Chairlift Maintenance Requirement
agency: JUSTICE, DEPARTMENT OF > FEDERAL PRISON SYSTEM / BUREAU OF PRISONS > USP LEAVENWORTH
description:
ELEVATOR AND CHAIRLIFT MAINTENANCE SERVICES FCI LEAVENWORTH 

 Category: Facilities, Subcategory: Facilities Maintenance and Repair NAICS: 561210 

 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations from eligible contractors for elevator and chairlift maintenance services in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. The requirement covers: - One traction elevator serving the Administrative Building. - One hydraulic elevator serving the Food Service/West Storeroom. - One Garaventa GSL Artira chairlift serving the Administrative Building entrance. Services include quarterly preventive maintenance, scheduled and unscheduled repairs, emergency callback services, service reporting, and annual inspection support as specified in the final SOW. The Government anticipates issuing one firm-fixed-price task order with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. 

 Place of Performance: FCI Leavenworth 1300 Metropolitan Avenue Leavenworth, Kansas 66048 

 Period of Performance - Base Period: January 1, 2027 - December 31, 2027 

 Option Year 1: January 1, 2028 - December 31, 2028 

 Option Year 2: January 1, 2029 - December 31, 2029 

 Option Year 3: January 1, 2030 - December 31, 2030 

 Option Year 4: January 1, 2031 - December 31, 2031 

 2. QUOTATION SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Submit quotations by the closing date and time identified in this RFQ to Contract Specialist, Kathleen Wood, kwood1@bop.gov. Quotations must include the following: A. Contractor Information Provide: - Legal business name, business address, and UEI. - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address. - Quotation validity period. - Acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments. B. Technical Service Approach Submit a technical service approach of no more than three pages addressing: 1. Equipment capability: Explain the ability to maintain and repair the traction elevator, hydraulic elevator, and Garaventa chairlift identified in the SOW. 2. Maintenance and inspection support: Describe the approach to quarterly preventive maintenance, service scheduling, reporting, and annual inspection support. 3. Staffing continuity: Describe qualified primary and backup technician coverage, availability during absences or concurrent service calls, and any subcontracting arrangements. 4. Emergency response: Explain the dispatch arrangements and available resources supporting the SOW's one-hour response requirement for trapped individuals and two-hour response requirement for other outages. 5. Parts and technical support: Explain access to necessary replacement parts, diagnostic tools, and technical support. 6. Institution coordination: Explain coordination of technician approvals, backup personnel, institution entry, escorts, tool control, and service scheduling. Provide a practical explanation of how the services will be performed. A general statement agreeing to comply with the SOW does not adequately describe the proposed approach. 

 C. Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar services performed within the past five years, including ongoing work. Government, commercial, and relevant subcontract performance may be submitted. For each example, provide: - Customer and project name. - Contract or order number, if available. - Performance dates. - Equipment and services covered. - Contractor's role. - Relevant performance results, including service reliability, emergency response, and resolution of performance problems. - Customer reference name, business email, and telephone number. Limit each example to one page. Contractors without relevant past performance should state that fact. 

 D. Pricing: Complete the pricing schedule below for the base period and all four option periods. Provide one annual firm-fixed price for each period covering all three units and all services included in the final SOW. Include all necessary labor, supervision, equipment, tools, travel, reporting, included repairs and parts, emergency callbacks, and inspection support. Identify any exceptions or proposed exclusions. Do not assume that contractor standard service-agreement exclusions apply. -

 E. Page Limits The three-page technical limit excludes contractor identification, past-performance examples, pricing, required representations, amendment acknowledgments, and exceptions. Use readable text of at least 11 points on standard letter-size pages. Technical pages exceeding the three-page limit will not be evaluated. Do not place additional technical narrative in excluded sections to circumvent the limit. 

 3. EVALUATION AND BASIS FOR SELECTION The Government will select the eligible Schedule contractor whose quotation meets the solicitation requirements and provides the best value considering: 1. Technical Service Approach. 2. Past Performance. 3. Price. Technical Service Approach is more important than Past Performance. Together, the nonprice factors are more important than Price. A. Technical Service Approach The Government will evaluate how well the proposed approach demonstrates the ability to maintain the identified equipment and meet the SOW. Considerations include equipment familiarity; maintenance and inspection-support planning; qualified primary and backup staffing; credible emergency dispatch and response coverage; access to parts and diagnostic support; and coordination with institution access requirements. These considerations explain the technical factor and are not separately weighted subfactors. B. Past Performance The Government will evaluate the relevance and quality of available past-performance information, including maintenance reliability, emergency response, and resolution of service problems.
